text:
Marta: Need a handoff for Helix Health POC (Private). They want VPC peering into our control plane + egress via their firewall/NAT. Can we draft a minimal network checklist I can send their cloud team?

Ken: Short list to request: full customer CIDRs, RTB IDs they'll modify, preferred connection (peering vs PrivateLink), NAT/firewall public IPs (EIP) for egress, and whether they need Route53 resolver or split-horizon DNS.

Marta: They provided CIDRs: 10.100.0.0/16 (apps), 10.101.0.0/22 (dc). They prefer peering.

Omar: Routing rules: customer RTB add route -> dest=10.220.0.0/16 (Redwood control plane) -> peering-conn-id. Our RTB add route -> dest=10.100.0.0/16 -> peering-conn-id. Confirm no overlapping prefixes.

Becca: Security: block propagated 0.0.0.0/0 into peered tables. We need TCP/443 inbound from their peered subnets to our control-plane ENIs. Prefer we provide ENI IPs; for POC we can accept peered CIDR but will tighten later. Also need NAT EIP(s) so we can allow outbound flows from models to external APIs.

Ken: DNS options: 1) VPC peering + Route53 Resolver inbound rule (they forward queries for our private zone to our resolver IPs) OR 2) PrivateLink + interface endpoints (requires per-AZ endpoints and endpoint SGs). For quick POC peering+resolver is usually faster.

Omar: AWS CLI snippets they can paste: on their side: aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc --destination-cidr-block 10.220.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0abc123
our side: aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0def --destination-cidr-block 10.100.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0abc123
then: aws ec2 modify-vpc-peering-connection-options --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0abc123 --accepter-peering-connection-options "{\"AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc\":true}" --requester-peering-connection-options "{\"AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc\":true}"

Becca: Firewall note: if their egress is NAT behind a firewall, ask them to whitelist our control-plane IPs for management callbacks and to allow outbound TLS to external hosts used by their workload. Provide list of outbound FQDNs if they need L7 allowlist.

Marta: Anything about IAM for automation? They asked about automating peering acceptance.

Ken: They can provide an assume-role ARN for us to accept the peering via CI, or accept manually. If they give a role, we need the role ARN and duration policy.

infra-bot: Deployment paused until peering is accepted and NAT EIP(s) are provided. Create ticket to collect RTB IDs, NAT EIP(s), and resolver IPs.

Marta: Perfect 1 I'll send this and ask for RTB IDs, NAT EIPs, and whether they want resolver setup or PrivateLink. Thanks all.
